text.p: Information technology firm Mutihouse NV said it had struck a deal with a group of utility companies aimed at keeping Multihouse afloat following its recent decision to seek court protection from creditors.
Multihouse said that in addition to the arrangements it had made with the utility companies it would try to seek out a company which was willing to take over Multihouse.
Multihouse was forced to seek court protection from creditors two weeks ago after the utility companies filed a claim for damages of some 170 million guilders against it.

Multihouse said it had now agreed to accept a liability of 5.9 million guilders towards the utility companies, of which five million guilders would be treated as a subordinated loan and 0.9 million would rank alongside other claims on the firm.
Additionally Multihouse has granted the utility companies options to acquire 2.8 million new ordinary shares in Multihouse at a price of 0.90 guilders per share.
Multihouse said if and when it is taken over, the purchaser would pay the utility companies the difference between the takeover price per share and 0.90 guilders.
Multihouse said it would continue to operate under court protection while it held talks with takeover candidates.
